title: CLI: generate tiered SLO configs + validate metric coverage by tier/endpoint/region
author: Aisha Bello
description: This PR adds CLI tooling to (1) generate tier-aware SLO config files from a canonical targets table and (2) validate metric coverage required to compute SLIs per tier/endpoint/region. This is intended to unblock the Tiered SLO + Error Budget program by making SLO config generation repeatable and preventing silent SLO data gaps (e.g., missing tier tags at ingest, missing streaming disconnect counters, or latency histograms not exported in a region). The generator produces configs compatible with the redwood SLO loader/schema introduced in redwood/pr-28438 (same field names and tier labeling). The validator checks that required metrics exist and are queryable for each config row, with guardrails to avoid cardinality explosions (no per-customer/per-model checks by default; validation is done at metric+label-key level). The CLI is intended for CI usage (fail fast) and for on-call debugging (show what’s missing + suggested instrumentation owners).
summary_of_changes: Added `sloctl` subcommands: `generate` (targets -> config) and `validate-metric-coverage` (config -> coverage report + exit code). Implemented a small metric catalog describing required series for availability, latency, and streaming reliability SLIs, including label-key expectations for `tier`, `region`, and `endpoint_class`. Added a Prometheus-compatible query backend (default) with a lightweight adapter interface so we can plug in Mimir later. Added CI-friendly outputs: JSON report and a human-readable table. Added docs and examples for Hosted vs Dedicated tiers and region scoping. Added unit tests for config generation, metric requirements expansion, and validation semantics (including exclusion cases like rate-limited requests).
user_facing_usage: Examples: `sloctl generate --targets ./data/tiered_slo_targets.csv --out ./configs/tiered_slos.yaml --default-window 30d` ; `sloctl validate-metric-coverage --config ./configs/tiered_slos.yaml --prom-url $PROM_URL --regions us-east-1,us-west-2,eu-west-1 --tier hosted --fail-on missing_required --format table` ; `sloctl validate-metric-coverage --config ./configs/tiered_slos.yaml --prom-url $PROM_URL --format json --out ./artifacts/slo_metric_coverage.json`
notes_on_validation_semantics: Validation checks for metric existence by running low-cost label discovery queries (e.g., `count by(__name__)(...)` / `label_values`) over a short lookback window (default 15m; configurable). It verifies: required metric names exist in the region(s); required label keys exist on the series (`tier`, `region`, and `endpoint_class`); and for histogram-based latency SLIs, that `_bucket`, `_sum`, `_count` series are present. It does NOT validate per-label-value cardinality by default (no `tier=dedicated` value checks unless `--check-label-values` is explicitly set), to avoid false negatives during partial rollout or sparse traffic. Streaming reliability validation expects either `api_stream_disconnect_total` (preferred) or the legacy `api_stream_ended_total{reason=...}` mapping; the report calls out which path is detected and recommends the preferred metric if only legacy is found.
generated_config_shape: Generated config output matches the redwood SLO schema expectations: name (stable), tier (hosted|dedicated), endpoint_class (chat|completions|embeddings|rerank|streaming), region (explicit), window (rolling, default 30d), slis (availability, latency, streaming where applicable), and exclusions (invalid_request, rate_limited, client_abort). The generator supports per-tier defaults and per-endpoint overrides (e.g., stricter latency targets for Dedicated chat in us-east-1 vs Hosted).
security_and_access_notes: The validator requires read-only access to the metrics backend. No customer identifiers are queried; queries are aggregated and scoped to region/metric/label keys. A `--dry-run` mode prints the planned queries for review. The CLI redacts Prom URLs containing credentials in logs and supports `--prom-bearer-token-file` to avoid env var leakage in CI logs.

review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we make sure we’re validating label *keys* not values by default? During rollout, Dedicated traffic in some regions will be sparse and this could flap CI. Also please document the lookback default and why.

Aisha Bello (author): Yep—default is label-key existence only. I added `--check-label-values` as opt-in (defaults false) and documented lookback defaults (15m) with rationale + override flag `--lookback`.

Thomas Baird: I’m worried about `label_values()` on high-cardinality metrics. Are we running it on anything with per-model labels? We should avoid accidentally pulling label sets on `model` or `customer_id` even if present.

Aisha Bello (author): Good call. Catalog explicitly scopes to metrics that are aggregated at gateway/routing/service level and we only request label values for a small allowlist of keys (`tier`, `region`, `endpoint_class`). Added a guard that errors if a query attempts to list non-allowlisted labels unless `--unsafe-allow-any-label` is provided (not for CI).

Logan Wright: Please align naming with the schema loader PR (redwood/pr-28438). Specifically, make sure endpoint_class values match what the loader expects and that the generator outputs stable `name` fields (no timestamps).

Aisha Bello (author): Updated endpoint_class enum to match loader (`chat`, `completions`, `embeddings`, `rerank`, `streaming`) and changed name generation to a deterministic slug: `{tier}.{region}.{endpoint_class}.{sli_set}`. Added a test that name stability holds across runs.
Jordan Lee: For the CI use-case, can we make the exit codes precise? I want to be able to gate on missing metrics vs temporary query errors/timeouts.

Aisha Bello (author): Added exit code mapping: 0 ok, 2 missing_required, 3 query_error, 4 invalid_config. Also added `--fail-on` policy with values `missing_required` (default) and `any` for strict mode.
Allison Grant: Approved after docs + guardrails updates.
Logan Wright: LGTM. This unblocks the rollout checklist item for metric coverage validation.
rollout_plan: Land CLI + docs. Next: wire `sloctl generate` and `sloctl validate-metric-coverage` into the redwood monorepo pipeline that owns SLO config artifacts (tracked in ENG-4926). Initial CI usage should run in warn-only mode (upload report artifact, do not fail) for 1 week, then move to fail-on missing_required once tier tagging at ingress is fully rolled out (redwood/pr-28411).
release_notes: Internal tooling: new `sloctl` commands for generating tiered SLO configs and validating metric coverage in Prometheus-compatible backends.
